We're hiring multiple Senior Product Managers across teams as we continue to scale.

At Vanta, our mission is to help businesses earn and prove trust.We believe that security should be monitored and verified continuously, and we empower companies to practice better security and prove it with ease. Vanta has a kind and talented team, and while some have prior security experience, many have been successful at Vanta without it.

As the Senior Product Manager for Integrations at Vanta, you will be responsible for the ongoing development of integrations across categories, driving direct customer impact through new integrations and expanded capabilities. Vanta currently manages a catalog of over 400 integrations that help customers continuously monitor their compliance and generate the evidence needed to satisfy audit. You’ll drive planning and delivery for a wide range of integration categories and capabilities, such as HRIS/IDP systems, cloud and security platforms, and ticketing systems, building on top of the integrations platform.

You’ll be part of Vanta’s Automation group, which owns how customers discover and connect to other platforms through integrations, use that data to power product experiences and tests, drive customers toward compliance-related security outcomes, and ultimately generate the evidence required for audit. You will operate in a few different modes to build your roadmap, balancing direction from other product teams, customer input, and your own prioritization framework to make the right investments. Plus, you will get wide exposure to most parts of Vanta’s products.

jobs.jd_full:
Waabi, founded by AI visionary Raquel Urtasun, is the leader in Physical AI. With a world-class team, we’re unlocking the next era of autonomous transportation with technology that’s powering commercial autonomous trucks and robotaxis. Waabi is backed by and partners with world leaders in AI, automotive, logistics, and deep tech.

With offices in Toronto, San Francisco, Dallas, and Pittsburgh, Waabi is growing quickly and looking for diverse, innovative and collaborative candidates who want to impact the world in a positive way. To learn more visit: www.waabi.ai

Waabi’s Commercial Product team defines and delivers the end-to-end commercial product that makes autonomous trucking deployable, scalable, and valuable to customers. We sit between autonomy, operations, business development, and customers, turning driverless capability into a real-world product that can be launched, sold, operated, and scaled.

As Waabi rapidly scales from commercial pilots to large-scale driverless deployments, this role serves as the critical integration layer between truck supply, customer commitments, expansion efforts, site activations, and autonomy capabilities. You will manage the execution of the commercial plan, proactively tracking dependencies and mitigating risks to drive clear commercial progress.

We are hiring a Senior Program Manager to own and align the single integrated commercialization plan, ensuring every element converges seamlessly.

While functional program leads manage their respective areas, you will integrate their milestones into the overarching commercial plan. Success relies on sound judgment: identifying critical dependencies, distinguishing real timeline slips, and resolving decision bottlenecks. A year from now, when leadership asks whether we are on track for a launch, a truck delivery or a customer commitment, the answer should be one page, current, and believed by every team on it.

What You’ll Do

You will own the integrated commercialization roadmap for trucking and the weekly operating cadence around it. This includes:

  • Build and own the integrated roadmap that ties customer commitments, OEM truck supply, autonomy and ODD readiness, lane and site activation, Mission Control, operations readiness and Account Management launches to dates, with the dependencies between them made explicit. You own the plan end to end.
  • Maintain the honest picture: the critical path, the slips, the risks and the decisions needed, surfaced early enough to act on and framed for the people who have to decide.
  • Lead the execution of key company milestones involving multiple departments at Waabi.
  • Run the operating cadence, including a weekly cross-functional Truck Program meeting.
  • Help establish repeatable frameworks, procedures, and decision loops that allow fast and efficient scale.
  • Produce executive-ready updates and program artifacts.
  • Communicate clearly with technical, operational, commercial and executive audiences that value first-principles thinking.

What Success Looks Like

Success in this role means the commercial plan converges on purpose rather than by heroics. Specifically, you will have:

  • Within 90 days, one integrated roadmap that Autonomy, Operations, Sales and Account Management believe, with the Truck Program meeting running off it.
  • A first driverless launch with no dependency discovered in the final month that was knowable in the first.
  • Leadership learning about a slip from you, with options, before they learn about it from a customer.
  • Decisions with a date, an owner and a record, so the same question is not re-decided in three meetings.

Qualifications Required

  • 7+ years in program or product leadership in a complex technical and operational environment (autonomous vehicles, automotive, aerospace, robotics, aviation, defense, logistics or other physical-world deployment).
  • Track record of integrating programs across teams you did not control, in a business with hardware, software, safety and operations in the loop.
  • Enough technical fluency to understand why an autonomy or hardware milestone slipped and whether the recovery plan is credible, without needing to be the engineer.
  • Separates facts, assumptions and risks in how you write and speak; comfortable telling senior people something they do not want to hear, early, with options.
  • Builds the minimum structure that works and removes or upgrades it when it stops working.
  • Executive-grade verbal and written communication; most of this role’s influence happens in documents and in how a problem is framed.
  • Set direction for a program others execute, with no direct reports, and being accountable for the outcome anyway.

Strongly Preferred

  • Ownership mentality: takes initiative and gets into the trenches with key stakeholders.
  • Varies the degree of detail to the audience and the moment.
  • Experience running a weekly holistic program review.
  • Experience taking a physical product from pilot to commercial deployment, where readiness gates and launch dates were real.
  • Experience working alongside a safety or systems-engineering function on go/no-go decisions.
  • Experience with OEM or supplier delivery schedules as a dependency in a commercial plan.
  • Zero-to-one program experience at an early-stage or scaling company.

Nice to have

  • Direct experience in autonomous trucking, freight or AV commercialization.
  • Experience working with operations and/or commercial teams.

Gusto’s Brand Studio is at an exciting inflection point. We’re scaling the team and building the systems to meet our growing ambition, from the brand refresh to increasingly complex, multi-channel integrated campaigns.

We’re looking for a Senior Creative Program Manager to be the connective tissue between Brand Studio and the cross-functional partners we build with: Marketing, PMM, R&D, and Legal. This role reports to the Manager of Creative Operations, who sets the operational roadmap and defines how the creative team interfaces with Marketing. You’ll independently execute against that roadmap: unblocking projects, managing cross-functional stakeholders, and driving timelines across standard tier-1/tier-2 launches and complex, multi-channel integrated campaigns, each with its own approval checkpoint and parallel workstream.

A core part of the role is helping stand up, optimize, and maintain the team’s project infrastructure  including the Brand Studio dashboard (an all-up project view for resourcing and capacity planning) and its task tracker, and driving consistent adoption and project management hygiene across the team and stakeholders. The Manager of Creative Operations leads the systems-level architecture; you’ll help build it out and own ongoing optimization and maintenance.

If you bring calm and clarity to fast-changing, multi-stakeholder work and you want to help shape, scale, and optimize the processes that let a growing in-house creative team meet this moment, this is your role.

Here’s what you’ll do day-to-day

  • Serve as the primary point of contact for cross-functional stakeholders (Marketing, PMM, Legal, R&D) across active projects including running daily/weekly updates, unblocking work, and escalating when needed
  • Build and maintain creative workback schedules, keeping the project source of truth (in partnership with Marketing) current as scope, deliverables, and deadlines shift
  • Manage vendor and agency relationships end to end including contractor paperwork, PO management, onboarding/access, and day-to-day production coordination with partners like STATE, Superside, and Uprise Art
  • Own the legal & compliance review pipeline for your projects including submitting requests, chasing disclosures and input, and keeping creative moving through legal feedback
  • Flag risks and dependencies early across creative projects, escalating to leadership before they become delivery problems
  • Schedule and run feedback checkpoints from internal crits and stakeholder reviews to leadership sign-offs, and consolidate feedback back to the team
  • Coordinate production logistics for shoots, agency staffing, on-site support, and the stakeholder management that comes with it
  • Help stand up, optimize, and maintain the team’s AI-enabled project infrastructure, including the Brand Studio dashboard and task tracker, and keep project management hygiene consistent across the team
  • Run retros and drive process improvements for better templates, tighter rituals, small workflow automations

Here’s what we’re looking for

  • 5–7 years of experience in creative, marketing, or brand production/project management — in-house or a blend of in-house and agency-side — with hands-on experience running point on multiple active projects, stakeholders, and vendors at once
  • Experience managing complex, multi-channel integrated campaigns with multiple channel owners,  including multiple approval checkpoints and parallel workstreams within a single project,  and balancing a portfolio of several such projects simultaneously
  • Experience building and maintaining workback schedules and/or project hubs (expertise doing this in Notion a plus) that a team relies on, and helping stand up, optimize, or drive adoption of project management infrastructure such as dashboards, task trackers, or similar systems across a team
  • Familiarity optimizing and maintaining AI-enabled tools and designing systems from scratch when needed; hands-on, daily use of AI tools for drafting, synthesis, and status updates
  • Comfort operating in ambiguity and shifting scope and experience in an agile, fast-changing environment (integrated campaigns, product marketing, or paid media).
  • Strong written and verbal communication; interest in running retros and improving process (templates, rituals, small workflow automations)
  • You bring order and calm to complexity. For example, a project without a clear owner, timeline, or next step doesn’t sit well with you.

Our cash compensation amount for this role is targeted at $146,000-$174,000 /yr in Denver & most remote locations, and $177,000-$211,000 /yr for San Francisco, Seattle & New York. Final offer amounts are determined by multiple factors, including candidate experience and expertise, and may vary from the amounts listed above.

Gusto has physical office spaces in Denver, San Francisco, and New York City. Employees who are based in those locations will be expected to work from the office on designated days approximately 2-3 days per week (or more depending on role). Note: The San Francisco office expectations encompass both the San Francisco and San Jose metro areas.

When approved to work from a location other than a Gusto office, a secure, reliable, and consistent internet connection is required. This includes non-office days for hybrid employees.
